cohort: The study included 6300 "low risk" pregnant women under midwife-led delivery care at a Japanese maternity hospital.
finding: Lateral birthing posture was associated with a lower incidence of perineal lacerations compared to supine, but fours posture was associated with a higher incidence of severe perineal lacerations.
